selection_approach: Four models were selected covering a range from simple linear baseline to optimized gradient boosting. Each model adds complexity incrementally so improvements can be clearly attributed to model capability.

models.reason_selected: Linear Regression is the standard baseline for regression problems. It is fast, interpretable and provides a minimum performance benchmark. Any model that cannot beat Linear Regression is not useful.
strengths: No risk of overfitting on large datasets
weaknesses: Assumes linear relationship between features and RUL

models.reason_selected: Random Forest is an ensemble of decision trees that can capture non-linear relationships. It is robust to noise and handles many features well — suitable for 95 engineered sensor features.
weaknesses: Prone to overfitting on training data
Slower to train than Linear Regression
Large memory usage with many trees

models.reason_selected: XGBoost uses gradient boosting to sequentially correct errors from previous trees. It includes built-in L1 and L2 regularization which reduces overfitting compared to Random Forest. It is the industry standard for tabular regression tasks.
weaknesses: Requires careful tuning for best results

models.reason_selected: Default XGBoost hyperparameters are generic. Randomized search over 25 combinations of learning rate, depth, subsample and regularization was used to find the best configuration for this specific aircraft engine dataset.
strengths: Best validation RMSE among all models
weaknesses: Longer training time due to search
Risk of over-tuning to validation set
